text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Conservative Disy party sends rebel mayor candidates to its disciplinary committee.
- Husband sought for pitchfork attack on wife.
- The National Council will be called to approve a six-point proposal on armaments today.
CYPRUS MAIL
- European Human Rights Court is to issue ruling today on refugee who has accused Turkey of violating her human rights.
- Pensioner sought after pitchfork attack on wife.
- Education officials struggle to dismiss poor science and maths test results.
- All-round scepticism is expressed on Rifkind's 10-point plan.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Moody's praises Laiki's (Popular Bank) strong financial ratios.
- Offshore registrations go up 19 percent.
- The Central Bank draws up plans for the full liberalisation of foreign investments.
HARAVGHI
- Britain cunningly omits to mention sovereignty in its 10-point plan on Cyprus.
- Government teachers go back to teaching at afternoon institutes.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Concerns are expressed at British positions on Cyprus. Greek Cypriot concerns are expressed over sovereignty, while Turkish Cypriot on guarantees.
- The government payroll for civil servants will go up by 35 million pounds ($74.7 million) next year after a 2.5 percent pay rise.
SIMERINI
- Britain circumvents sovereignty in its 10-point proposal.
- Outgoing United Nations Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali wants some 1000 missing persons from 1974 declared 'presumed dead'.
